children: Astrotech reported results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, with revenue of $913,000 and a net loss of $14.4 million. The company recorded gross profit of $217,000 and total operating expenses of $14.4 million, and held $11.3 million in cash and short-term investments at year-end. Management highlighted product launches and a new subsidiary focused on potential lunar infrastructure initiatives.
Revenue: $913,000 for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026.
Gross profit: $217,000 for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026.
Total operating expenses: $14.355 million for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 (decline of 6% versus prior year).
Loss from operations before income taxes: $(14.423) million for fiscal 2026.
Net loss: $(14.427) million; basic and diluted net loss per common share: $(8.49).
Cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments: $11.334 million as of June 30, 2026 ($8.387M cash; $2.947M short-term investments).
Product deployments: TRACER 1000 deployed in approximately 37 locations across 16 countries spanning the United States, Europe and Asia.
New product launch: Introduced the Labrador ruggedized Handheld Gas Chromatograph for field volatile organic compound analysis.
Strategic initiative: Board approved formation of Lunar Power and Light to pursue potential lunar resource development and autonomous lunar industrial infrastructure opportunities.

Planned technology focus for lunar initiative: Evaluation of infrastructure technologies to support semiconductor processing, advanced and quantum computing manufacturing, lunar power generation, mining, chemical manufacturing, transportation and equipment leasing on the Moon.

Subsidiary business model: Continued operation through wholly owned subsidiaries (1st Detect, AgLAB, Pro-Control, EN-SCAN, and Lunar Power and Light) leveraging mass spectrometry and related technologies for specialized markets.
